problem.text: In the rectangular parallelepiped shown, $AB=3$, $BC=1$, and $CG=2$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{FG}$. What is the volume of the rectangular pyramid with base $BCHE$ and apex $M$?

steps.title: Where to start: cut the box, then subtract
steps.body: The base $BCHE$ is slanted, so the pyramid's height is awkward to find directly. Instead, notice that the slanted rectangle $BCHE$ runs from the bottom right edge $BC$ to the top left edge $EH$, so it cuts the box into two equal halves. The pyramid sits inside the upper half, the one containing $F$, $G$ and $M$.

your_turn.prompt: What is the volume of the box, and of each half?
your_turn.answer: The box is $3 \cdot 1 \cdot 2 = 6$, so each half is $3$.

steps.title: Split the upper half into three pyramids
steps.body: The upper half is a triangular prism: its front end is triangle $BFE$ (half of the front face $ABFE$), its back end is triangle $CGH$, and its length is $BC = 1$. Point $M$ lies on edge $FG$ of this prism. Joining $M$ to every corner splits the prism into three pyramids with apex $M$: our pyramid on base $BCHE$, one on the front triangle $BFE$, and one on the back triangle $CGH$.

your_turn.prompt: What is the area of triangle $BFE$?
your_turn.answer: It is a right triangle with legs $BF = 2$ and $FE = 3$, so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 2 = 3$.

steps.title: Height of the small pyramids
steps.body: The height of pyramid $M$-$BFE$ is the distance from $M$ to the front face, measured straight back along edge $FG$. The back pyramid $M$-$CGH$ matches it exactly. Careful: a pyramid's volume is $\frac{1}{3} \cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$, not $\frac{1}{6}$.

your_turn.prompt: How far is $M$ from the front face $ABFE$?
your_turn.answer: $\frac{1}{2}$, because $FG$ runs from front to back with length $BC = 1$, and $M$ is its midpoint.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Each small pyramid has volume $\frac{1}{3} \cdot 3 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$. Take both of them away from the half-box.
$$3 - \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 2$$
The answer is **(E)** $2$.

wrong_choices.A: $1$ comes from using $\frac{1}{6}$ instead of $\frac{1}{3}$ in the pyramid volume formula: base $BCHE$ times the height from $M$ is $6$, and $\frac{1}{6}$ of that is $1$. A pyramid is always $\frac{1}{3} \cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$.
